title: Assumption tracing & data-lineage review — Optimize cost model
body:
Purpose:
This is a working review doc to trace every major assumption used by the Optimize cost model v3 (sheet:1A2b3C_optimize-cost-v3), validate data sources, and define the calibration steps required for Finance sign-off. The goal is to create a reproducible lineage from raw telemetry -> processed inputs -> model outputs so that finance is comfortable with the unit economics and we can rapidly re-run calibrations when upstream data changes.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Most numbers come from two primary telemetry sets: token telemetry (prod-token-agg) and instance utilization traces (gpu-usage-hourly).
- Secondary inputs: on-demand spot pricing history (cloud-billing/spot-history.csv), persistent storage egress/tiering samples, and our internal quantization benchmark results (quant-bench/2025-q1).
- Key open risks: prefix caching hit-rate extrapolation for long-tail workloads, mismatch between sampled eval prompt lengths and production shape, and how we amortize prefetch/warm-up costs for cold-start bursts.
- Recommendation: finance sign-off contingent on (A) re-running calibration with 30-day rolling production token distribution (B) acceptance of a conservative KV cache hit baseline (10% lower than current estimate) and (C) explicit write-up of amortization methodology for reserved capacity.

Data sources (where each input comes from):
1) Token-level cost & length distribution
   - Source: prod-token-agg (BigQuery table), exported weekly to sheet:1A2b3C_token_samples
   - Fields used: token_in, token_out, prompt_seq_len, response_seq_len, session_id
   - Notes: current sampling window is 14 days; Finance requested 30d for seasonality. We need to document sampling bias for weekends/PLG spikes.

2) KV / prefix cache hit rates
   - Source: runtime-cache-metrics (Prometheus -> long-term store)
   - Fields used: cache_hits, cache_misses, prefix_id, model_version
   - Current assumption in model: aggregate hit rate = 35% (derived from internal A/B on 2 customers and headroom projection)
   - Risk: A/B customers are more chatty; production average may be 20-25%. Recommend defaulting to 25% for finance scenario and adding a "best-case / base / conservative" trio.

3) Batching efficiency and tail-latency policy effect
   - Source: serving-runtime/batching-sim-outputs.csv (synthetic runs) and live traces from dedicated pools (dedicated-batches/2025-11)
   - Model input: tokens per batch, effective throughput (tokens/sec), average latency percentile uplift
   - Notes: synthetic sim currently uses optimistic 10% higher throughput than observed in dedicated pools during peak. Calibration step: apply correction factor from last 2 live peak days (Nov 2025).

4) Hardware pricing & utilization
   - Source: cloud-billing/spot-history.csv, reserved-costs.xls (procurement)
   - Fields used: spot hourly, reserved amortized monthly, GPU_utilization_pct
   - Amortization: reserved capacity allocated across committed qps curve; need explicit formula in sheet cell R45 and narrative for finance.

5) Quantization and memory tradeoffs
   - Source: quant-bench/2025-q1 results, PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quant/834
   - Metrics: throughput delta, accuracy regression (p50), memory footprint change
   - Current assumption: 4-bit quantized = 1.8x throughput, 2% p50 regress. Data is noisy for long sequences. Recommendation: include a 95% CI band for quality/regression impact.

Calibration methodology (how we turn raw data into model inputs):
- Step 0: lock the versions of the datasets used (sheet id references above). We must snapshot BigQuery queries as view IDs and store them in the Confluence page CONF-4567.
- Step 1: expand token sample window to 30d and stratify by customer tier (free / self-serve / enterprise) to avoid PLG bias. Produce per-tier seq-length histograms.
- Step 2: compute KV hit baseline from rolling 60-day sliding window, then derive three scenarios: conservative (-15pp), base (observed), aggressive (+10pp). Update model to allow scenario toggles.
- Step 3: re-weight synthetic batching sims by real-world peak-day throughput ratios (peak-day / median-day). We will recompute tokens/sec curves and re-evaluate cost-per-token.
- Step 4: reconcile GPU_utilization_pct with billing logs (cloud-billing) to ensure utilization decimal rounding is not overstating effective throughput.
- Step 5: sensitivity sweep: run model across grid of sequence lengths (16, 64, 256, 1024), cache hit rates (10, 25, 35, 50), and quant profiles (fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit) and capture cost delta table in sheet:1A2b3C_sensitivity_grid.

Finance sign-off checklist (required to present to Finance):
- [ ] Data snapshots attached (BigQuery view ids + CSV exports).
- [ ] 30-day token distribution applied and committed in the sheet.
- [ ] KV hit-rate scenario defined with justification (source queries + sample size).
- [ ] Amortization narrative for reserved capacity and one worked example (numbers in row R45:R52).
- [ ] Sensitivity grid included and highlighted conservative scenario as primary.
- [ ] Explicit note on where headroom / buffers are included (we currently add 7% buffer for misc egress and throttles; must justify).
- [ ] Sign-off line for Finance with contact (Rafael Ortega) and acceptance thresholds (< +/- 5% on primary unit costs for final approval).

Open questions & known issues:
- How do we treat cold-start prefill cost? Current model spreads prefill across first 1k requests; on enterprise burst workloads that understates cost. Owner: Samir (action below).
- Should we include storage egress tier transitions (hot -> warm -> cold) in the per-token cost, or treat as separate line item? Finance prefers separate line items but operations prefers embedded amortization. Note: embedding retrieval workloads push egress significantly.
- Quantization accuracy: bench dataset lacks long conversation contexts (>2048). Need targeted benchmark for long-context models. Owner: Priya.
- Does the cost model include the incremental cost of tracing/observability (percent CPU/RAM per host)? Currently adds 1.2% to infra; need concrete profiler numbers.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Maya: produce 30-day token distribution export and update token_samples sheet — due 2026-02-27.
- Samir: produce cold-start amortization proposal (3 variants: front-loaded, linear, per-request) with example calculations — due 2026-03-03.
- Priya: run quant-bench long-context job (2k and 4k token runs) and upload CSVs; add accuracy tables to model — due 2026-02-28.
- Rafael (Finance): review conservative KV baseline and confirm acceptance criteria for sign-off (target: <5% variance) — due 2026-03-06.
- Emily: re-run batching sim with corrected peak-day multiplier and push new sim CSV to drive — due 2026-02-24.

Acceptance criteria for final sheet (what Finance needs to see to stamp):
- All inputs are pinned to sources with snapshots (no ad-hoc numbers).
- Conservative scenario explained and documented as the primary finance scenario.
- Sensitivity runs attached and show worst-case cost delta not exceeding 12% (if >12%, must label as "high variance" and indicate mitigation).
- Three amortization examples for reserved capacity with explicit math.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is intentionally opinionated: I biased the baseline slightly conservative on cache hit-rate because our PLG sample skewed high. If Ops has hard logs to contest that, we'll revise.
- Keep an eye on the "misc buffer" line — it accumulated as a hedge and needs to be reduced once we have stronger egress numbers.
- We should convert the sensitivity grid into a tiny dashboard in Console so sales/solutions can play with scenarios. That should be a separate ticket (OPT-920?).

Appendix (quick references):
- sheet:1A2b3C_optimize-cost-v3 (main model)
- sheet:1A2b3C_token_samples (token-level exports)
- sheet:1A2b3C_sensitivity_grid (sweep outputs)
- conf:CONF-4567-assumption-trace (versioned queries)
- jira:OPT-912 (Epic for cost-model revamp)

If you're reviewing: please comment inline on the sheet for specific formula questions. For high-level objections, call out which input you disagree with and provide the alternative source or numbers.

Maya
(Notes captured during product/finance sync 2026-02-20)
